synonyms: Scutellaria integrifolia var. brevifolia A.Gray ex E.Hall
taxonomic_note: Accepted by Kew/POWO; learner stays species-level.
look_here_first: First look at the plant base and leaf tips. Wright's skullcap is a low bushy perennial with many stems from a persistent base and small entire leaves with rounded/obtuse tips. Its hairs are minute and the calyx can look nearly smooth to the naked eye. Then confirm the larger upward-curving blue-violet corolla and visorlike skullcap calyx.

project_inclusion.range_basis: BONAP/NAPA provides a county-level map for Scutellaria wrightii. Hays County — UT Plant Resources Center's Purola Preserve natural flora lists S. wrightii among naturally occurring plants. Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Lamiaceae specimen index includes S. wrightii. Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center publishes a dedicated Williamson County treatment for S. wrightii.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Nursery and garden occurrences are not used as native-county proof. The PASS rests on native-flora/herbarium/county-treatment evidence.

best_field_traits: perennial herb, taprooted, several-many-stemmed at the base, usually 10–20 cm tall
stems four-sided, densely puberulent with minute sessile glandular hairs
leaves opposite and decussate, short-petiolate, ovate to elliptic
leaf margins entire and tips rounded/obtuse
leafy raceme with paired axillary flowers, often oriented mainly to one side
calyx two-lipped with a projecting visorlike scutellum; puberulent but often smoother-looking than S. drummondii
corolla mostly 13–18 mm long, with a cylindric tube that curves upward and a violet throat
fruit produces four small minutely warty nutlets
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Scutellaria drummondii: S. drummondii is an annual with acute-tipped leaves, more conspicuous glandular hairs, shorter pedicels (about 1–1.2 mm) and smaller corollas (about 5.5–10 mm). S. wrightii is perennial/bushy, round-tipped and larger-flowered. Scutellaria ovata: S. ovata is much taller and rhizomatous, with large triangular-ovate leaves having truncate/subcordate bases and crenate margins; its corolla is about 21–25 mm.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. drummondii is an annual with acute-tipped leaves, more conspicuous glandular hairs, shorter pedicels (about 1–1.2 mm) and smaller corollas (about 5.5–10 mm). S. wrightii is perennial/bushy, round-tipped and larger-flowered. S. ovata is much taller and rhizomatous, with large triangular-ovate leaves having truncate/subcordate bases and crenate margins; its corolla is about 21–25 mm.
